newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour jumps 6 points, closes in on govt - poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour jumps 6 points, closes in on govt - poll.

text.p: A week before New Zealand's general election the main opposition Labour Party has dramatically closed the gap on the ruling conservative National Party, according to an opinion poll published on Saturday.

The poll in the Auckland newspaper "The New Zealand Herald" taken in the week to October 2 showed Labour had jumped almost six points to 27.7 percent in a week, while National had dropped 2.8 percentage points to 34 percent.
Among other opposition parties, economic nationalist New Zealand First was down four at 14 percent while the five-party left-wing Alliance grouping was up 0.6 of a point at 12.6 percent.

National's likely coalition partners remained below the crucial five percent threshold at which parties who do not win a constituency seat qualify for seats from the party list under rules for the proportional representation system adopted for this election.
Free-market ACT New Zealand was up 0.5 percent to 4.6 percent while the morals-based Christian Coalition was down marginally at four percent from 4.3 percent previously.
The government's current coalition partner United New Zealand, whose Ohariu-Belmont candidate Peter Dunne seems certain to win his seat, scored less than one percent support.
If the poll was reflected in support in the general election on October 12, National would win 46 seats, Labour 37, New Zealand First 19, the Alliance 17 and United one.
The Alliance has ruled out entering a coalition after the election but has said it might support a minority government that did not include National.
New Zealand First has kept its options open but is leaning towards a deal with Labour.
The poll would give a Labour-New Zealand First-Alliance arrangement 73 seats in the 120 seat single chamber parliament.
It would also bring a Labour-New Zealand First or Labour- Alliance deal within striking distance of the 60 seats needed to command a majority.
The poll of 850 voters taken by Waikato University showed the level of undecided voters had dropped to 11.5 percent from 13 percent the previous week.

The poll was taken during week which saw Labour leader Helen Clark emerge as the clear winner of the first TV1 leaders debate and controversy over changes to the format for next Monday's debate. It showed support for National picking up towards the end of the polling period after dipping earlier.
